(1) CoT Curation: We extend the VideoRFT pipeline to generate timestamp-annotated CoTs where each reasoning step references specific frame intervals, verified by a video grounding model. (2) Temporal Grounding Reward: We design a novel reward component that scores the temporal precision of cited evidence—using IoU between model-predicted timestamps in reasoning traces and ground-truth event intervals. This reward is combined with answer-correctness and semantic-consistency signals. (3) Architecture: A lightweight temporal pointer head is added to predict frame-interval citations alongside text generation. Experiments: We evaluate on temporal QA benchmarks (ActivityNet-QA, NExT-QA, Charades-STA), measuring both answer accuracy and temporal grounding precision, ablating reward components and comparing against VideoRFT baselines to demonstrate improved temporal faithfulness.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward Shaping for Fine-Grained Temporal Grounding in Video Reasoning via Timestamp-Anchored Chain-of-Thought
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT advances video reasoning through semantic consistency rewards, it lacks explicit supervision for precise temporal grounding—knowing *when* specific events occur is critical for answering causal and procedural questions (e.g., 'What caused the fall at 0:23?'). Current CoT pipelines treat video holistically, producing reasoning chains that reference events vaguely without temporal anchors, limiting interpretability and downstream localization tasks.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT paradigm with timestamp-anchored CoT generation and a temporal grounding reward. First, we build a CoT curation pipeline that forces reasoning chains to include explicit timestamp spans (e.g., '[12s-15s]: subject picks up object') using a frame-caption alignment module. Second, we design a temporal consistency reward composed of: (1) an IoU-based reward measuring overlap between model-predicted timestamps and ground-truth event spans, and (2) a causal-ordering reward penalizing chains where cited timestamps contradict logical event ordering. We construct a 50K dataset pairing procedural/causal video QA with timestamp-annotated CoTs from Ego4D and HiREST.

Experiments: We evaluate on temporal grounding benchmarks (QVHighlights, Charades-STA), procedural QA (HiREST, EgoSchema), and causal reasoning (NExT-QA), comparing against VideoRFT and standard GRPO baselines, with ablations on each reward component.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward-Shaping for Fine-Grained Temporal Grounding in Video Reasoning via Timestamp-Anchored Chain-of-Thought
description: Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, it does not explicitly enforce that the model's reasoning chain correctly references *when* in the video evidence occurs. Models may produce plausible-sounding CoTs that cite incorrect temporal segments, a subtle but critical failure mode for applications like video QA, surveillance analysis, and sports analytics. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT pipeline with timestamp-anchored CoT annotations and a temporal grounding reward. During SFT, we extend CoT generation to require explicit timestamp citations (e.g., '[t=12.3s] the player passes the ball') using a pipeline that aligns LLM-generated reasoning steps to video frames via a vision-language aligner. During RL, we design a composite reward combining: (1) answer correctness, (2) semantic consistency (from VideoRFT), and (3) a novel temporal precision reward measuring IoU between cited timestamps and ground-truth relevant segments derived from dense video captions. Planned Experiments: We evaluate on temporal reasoning benchmarks (NExT-QA, ActivityNet-QA, TimeIT, Charades-STA) and introduce a new diagnostic suite measuring timestamp citation accuracy vs. answer accuracy correlation. Ablations isolate contribution of each reward component and test generalization to zero-shot temporal grounding tasks.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward Shaping via Fine-Grained Temporal Grounding for Video Reasoning in MLLMs
description:
Problem: VideoRFT improves video reasoning via semantic-consistency rewards, but treats temporal alignment as implicit. Models can produce correct answers with temporally misaligned reasoning—citing wrong timestamps or confusing event order—without penalty. This limits causal and procedural understanding requiring precise temporal grounding.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, extending the RFT framework with explicit temporal grounding rewards. Beyond semantic consistency, we design a Temporal Grounding Reward (TGR) that evaluates whether the model's chain-of-thought citations (extracted via structured reasoning tags like <timestamp>, <event_span>) align with ground-truth temporal annotations. TGR combines: (1) a span-overlap score between cited and annotated event intervals (IoU-based), and (2) a causal-ordering score penalizing reversed event sequences in reasoning chains. We curate a temporally-annotated extension of VideoRFT-RL-310K by automatically aligning CoT reasoning steps to video segments using an off-the-shelf temporal grounding model, yielding ~85K temporally-annotated examples. Training uses a composite reward: accuracy + semantic consistency (from VideoRFT) + TGR.

Experiments: We evaluate on (1) standard video QA benchmarks (NExT-QA, EgoSchema, MVBench), (2) temporal reasoning benchmarks (TemporalBench, ActivityNet-Causal), and (3) a new diagnostic probing suite measuring timestamp citation accuracy. Ablations isolate each reward component's contribution.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward-Guided Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Dense Temporal Grounding in Long-Form Videos
description: Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, it does not explicitly address fine-grained temporal localization—pinpointing when specific events occur in long videos (e.g., 10-60 minutes). Existing MLLMs struggle to produce accurate timestamps and temporal spans, limiting practical applications like video search and highlight detection. Proposed Method: We extend the RFT paradigm with a temporally-grounded reward framework. First, we construct a CoT dataset (TemporalCoT-50K) where reasoning chains explicitly reference timestamped evidence segments, generated by prompting a reasoning LLM with ASR transcripts, dense captions, and scene boundaries, then validated by a video MLLM. During RL, we introduce two complementary rewards: (1) a temporal precision reward that scores predicted event timestamps against ground-truth intervals using IoU-based metrics, and (2) a causal-chain reward that verifies the logical ordering of cited temporal evidence within the reasoning trace. The model learns to anchor its reasoning to specific video moments rather than holistic content. Experiments: We evaluate on QVHighlights, Charades-STA, ActivityNet-QA (temporal subset), and EgoSchema using temporal grounding accuracy, mean IoU, and R@1. Ablations isolate contributions of each reward component and CoT grounding quality, with comparisons against VideoRFT and state-of-the-art temporal grounding baselines.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Causal and Counterfactual Video Reasoning via Temporal Intervention Rewards
description: Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, models still struggle with causal and counterfactual temporal reasoning—understanding not just what happened, but why, and what would have happened under different conditions. Existing benchmarks and rewards do not specifically incentivize this deeper causal understanding. Proposed Method: We extend the RFT paradigm with a temporally-aware causal reasoning framework. First, we construct a counterfactual CoT dataset by augmenting video QA pairs with 'what-if' interventions: systematically masking or replacing temporal segments and asking models to reason about altered outcomes. Second, we introduce a Temporal Intervention Reward (TIR) that scores model outputs based on (1) causal consistency—whether predicted counterfactual outcomes align with physically plausible temporal interventions, and (2) temporal directionality—penalizing answers that confuse cause-effect ordering. The reward is computed via a lightweight temporal causal graph extractor trained on annotated video segments. Third, we design a curriculum RL strategy that progressively introduces longer temporal dependencies and more complex interventions. Planned Experiments: We evaluate on NExT-QA (causal/temporal splits), Causal-VidQA, and a new CounterfactualVideo-QA benchmark we construct. Ablations compare TIR against semantic-consistency rewards from VideoRFT, and analyze reasoning chain quality via human evaluation of causal coherence.

title: TemporalChain: Disentangling Causal and Temporal Reasoning in Video MLLMs via Structured Reward Decomposition
description:
Problem: VideoRFT treats video reasoning holistically, but temporal reasoning (understanding event ordering, duration, simultaneity) and causal reasoning (understanding cause-effect chains) are fundamentally distinct cognitive skills that may conflict during joint optimization. Current reward signals cannot identify which reasoning type is failing, making targeted improvement impossible.

Proposed Method: We propose TemporalChain, which decomposes video reasoning into three explicit sub-chains: (1) temporal grounding chain identifying when events occur, (2) causal attribution chain explaining why events occur, and (3) synthesis chain integrating both for final answers. We introduce a structured reward decomposition with three separate verifiable reward signals: temporal accuracy (evaluated via timestamp prediction against ground-truth event boundaries), causal plausibility (evaluated via counterfactual consistency—would swapping cause/effect break the reasoning?), and answer correctness. We train using multi-objective GRPO where each reward component has an adaptive weight updated based on per-sample difficulty. CoT data is augmented with explicit temporal and causal annotations using structured tags.

Experiments: We evaluate on (1) existing benchmarks from VideoRFT, (2) NExT-QA focusing on causal/temporal splits separately, (3) a new diagnostic benchmark with controlled temporal/causal perturbations. Ablations isolate contributions of each reward component. We demonstrate TemporalChain improves causal reasoning by 8%+ over VideoRFT while maintaining temporal accuracy.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Causal and Counterfactual Video Reasoning via Intervention-Based Rewards
description: Problem: While VideoRFT advances general video reasoning, MLLMs still struggle specifically with causal and counterfactual reasoning — understanding not just what happened, but why it happened and what would have occurred under different conditions. Existing rewards and CoT pipelines do not explicitly incentivize this type of interventional thinking. Method: We propose TemporalRFT, which extends the RFT paradigm with a dedicated causal-counterfactual reasoning framework. First, we construct a CoT curation pipeline that generates causal chains and counterfactual alternatives (e.g., 'if the actor had not opened the door, then...') by prompting a reasoning LLM with structured causal graphs extracted via scene parsing. Second, we design an intervention-consistency reward: during RL, the model is presented with synthetically edited video clips (objects removed, events reordered using video editing tools) and penalized when its counterfactual predictions contradict observable evidence in the modified video. Third, we introduce a causal-grounding reward that checks whether identified causes temporally precede effects in the model's chain-of-thought. Experiments: We evaluate on NExT-QA, Causal-VidQA, STAR benchmark, and a newly constructed CounterfactualVideo-QA dataset with 15K human-annotated counterfactual questions. Ablations compare reward components and CoT quality against VideoRFT baselines.

title: TemporalRFT: Counterfactual Temporal Reasoning in Videos via Causal Intervention Rewards
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT advances video reasoning through chain-of-thought supervision and semantic-consistency rewards, it primarily rewards alignment between reasoning and observed visual evidence. This leaves a critical gap: models still struggle with counterfactual and causal temporal reasoning (e.g., 'What would happen if action X occurred at timestamp T instead of Y?'), which requires understanding causal structure rather than merely describing observed sequences.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT paradigm with a counterfactual causal intervention reward. During the RL phase, alongside standard correctness rewards, we introduce a causal-consistency reward that evaluates whether the model's reasoning correctly tracks causal dependencies when presented with counterfactually-edited video clips (generated via video inpainting/editing models). We construct a counterfactual video QA dataset by systematically editing key causal events in existing videos and verifying that model reasoning changes appropriately. Additionally, we design a temporal intervention prompting strategy that forces CoT reasoning to explicitly identify causal anchors before answering.

Experiments: (1) Evaluate on existing benchmarks (NExT-QA causal split, Causal-VidQA, EgoSchema); (2) Introduce a new Counterfactual Video Reasoning benchmark with 15K edited clip pairs; (3) Ablate reward components and compare against VideoRFT and standard VLMs; (4) Analyze whether causal reasoning generalizes to out-of-distribution temporal perturbations.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward-Shaping for Fine-Grained Temporal Localization in Video Reasoning via Timestamp-Anchored Chain-of-Thought
description: Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, it lacks explicit grounding in *when* key events occur. Models may produce plausible but temporally vague reasoning (e.g., 'later in the video') without pinpointing precise timestamps, limiting applicability to temporal grounding tasks like moment retrieval, step localization in procedural videos, and causal event ordering. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT pipeline with timestamp-anchored CoT supervision and a novel temporal precision reward. During SFT, we curate a 50K dataset where each reasoning step explicitly cites temporal intervals (e.g., '[0:12-0:18]: agent picks up object, causing...') using a pipeline that combines ASR, optical flow change-point detection, and an LLM to scaffold temporally-grounded CoTs. During RL, we add a timestamp accuracy reward computed as the IoU between cited intervals in the model's reasoning chain and ground-truth annotation intervals, combined with answer correctness. This dual reward incentivizes both correct answers and temporally-faithful reasoning traces. Experiments: We evaluate on temporal grounding benchmarks (QVHighlights, Charades-STA), procedural QA (COIN, CrossTask), and causal video QA (NExT-QA), comparing against VideoRFT and non-temporal CoT baselines, with ablations isolating the timestamp reward contribution.

title: TemporalRFT: Counterfactual Temporal Reasoning for Video MLLMs via Causal Intervention Rewards
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT advances video reasoning through chain-of-thought and semantic consistency rewards, it does not explicitly train models to understand causal-temporal dependencies — specifically, whether a model truly understands *why* event B follows event A versus merely recognizing their co-occurrence. This limits robustness on causal reasoning tasks like accident analysis, procedural understanding, and counterfactual prediction.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT pipeline with counterfactual temporal reasoning. During RL, we generate counterfactual video variants by temporally shuffling, masking, or replacing key event segments using a video editing model. We then introduce a Causal Intervention Reward (CIR) that scores model responses based on (1) correctly predicting outcome changes under counterfactual interventions, and (2) identifying which temporal segments are causally necessary for the original outcome. A contrastive CoT dataset is curated where reasoning chains explicitly trace causal dependencies between events.

Experiments: We evaluate on (1) existing benchmarks: NExT-QA causal splits, STAR, Causal-VidQA; (2) a new CounterfactualVideo-QA benchmark we construct with GPT-4o-generated counterfactual questions across 5K videos; (3) ablations comparing CIR vs. semantic-consistency reward from VideoRFT. We expect significant gains on causal/counterfactual splits while maintaining competitive performance on descriptive QA tasks.

title: TemporalRFT: Counterfactual Temporal Reasoning in Videos via Causal Intervention Rewards
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, MLLMs still struggle with counterfactual temporal reasoning—understanding how changing the order, duration, or presence of events would alter outcomes. This is crucial for causal understanding in domains like surgical training, sports analytics, and accident reconstruction, yet no existing RFT framework explicitly targets this capability.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT paradigm with counterfactual video reasoning. First, we construct a counterfactual CoT dataset by synthetically perturbing videos (frame reordering, segment removal, temporal reversal) paired with LLM-generated causal reasoning chains explaining why outcomes change. Second, during RL, we design a Causal Intervention Reward (CIR) that scores model outputs by verifying: (1) correct identification of the manipulated temporal segment, (2) logically consistent causal explanation linking intervention to outcome change, and (3) consistency with unperturbed video baseline reasoning. The CIR uses a lightweight temporal graph verifier to check causal chain validity against a ground-truth event dependency graph extracted via scene parsing.

Experiments: We evaluate on existing benchmarks (NExT-QA, Causal-VidQA, EgoSchema) plus a new CounterfactualVideo-QA benchmark we construct with 15K human-verified counterfactual pairs across surgical, cooking, and sports domains. Ablations isolate contributions of each reward component and counterfactual augmentation strategy.

title: TemporalRFT: Counterfactual Temporal Reasoning in Videos via Causal Intervention Rewards
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT advances video reasoning through chain-of-thought and semantic-consistency rewards, it does not explicitly train models to reason about counterfactual temporal causality — i.e., 'what would have happened if event X occurred differently?' This causal reasoning capability is critical for applications like accident analysis, procedural planning, and anomaly detection, yet remains largely unaddressed in video MLLMs.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT paradigm with counterfactual causal reasoning. First, we build a counterfactual video CoT dataset by prompting reasoning LLMs with structured video descriptions plus causal graph annotations (extracted via off-the-shelf tools), generating 'intervention' scenarios and their consequences. Second, we design a causal intervention reward that scores model responses by verifying logical consistency of predicted counterfactual outcomes against known video ground truth (e.g., using physics simulators or annotated causal chains). Third, we introduce a temporal contrastive reward that penalizes the model when it produces the same counterfactual prediction regardless of which event is intervened upon, forcing genuine causal sensitivity.

Experiments: We evaluate on (1) existing benchmarks like NExT-QA and Causal-VidQA, (2) a new counterfactual video QA benchmark we construct from cooking and driving datasets, and (3) out-of-domain generalization to anomaly explanation tasks. We ablate each reward component and compare against VideoRFT and standard SFT baselines.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward-Shaping for Fine-Grained Temporal Localization in Video Reasoning
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, models still struggle with precise temporal grounding—answering 'when' questions requires not just semantic understanding but pinpointing exact timestamps where evidence occurs. Current semantic-consistency rewards don't explicitly penalize temporally mislocalized reasoning chains, leading to plausible-sounding but temporally vague explanations.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RL phase with a temporal localization reward alongside semantic rewards. During training, the model is required to produce reasoning chains that cite specific frame ranges (e.g., 'frames 30-45 show...') as part of its CoT. We design a composite reward: (1) a temporal IoU reward comparing predicted frame spans against annotated evidence windows, (2) a causal-ordering reward penalizing chains where cited temporal evidence contradicts the narrative order, and (3) the original answer-correctness reward. For CoT curation, we extend the VideoRFT pipeline to extract temporal evidence annotations from structured video metadata and human-annotated QA pairs with timestamps.

Experiments: We evaluate on temporally-demanding benchmarks including NExT-QA, ActivityNet-QA, and newly collected temporal grounding QA splits. Ablations isolate contribution of each reward component. We further analyze whether explicit temporal grounding in reasoning chains transfers to zero-shot temporal video grounding tasks, demonstrating cross-task generalization.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Long-Horizon Video Reasoning via Hierarchical Temporal Credit Assignment
description:
Problem: VideoRFT and similar approaches treat video reasoning holistically, but struggle with long-horizon videos (>5 minutes) where temporal credit assignment — determining which specific frames or temporal segments contributed to a correct reasoning chain — remains unsolved. Standard outcome-based rewards provide no gradient signal about which temporal reasoning steps were correct, causing the model to learn spurious temporal correlations.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which extends VideoRFT with a hierarchical temporal credit assignment mechanism. First, we segment long videos into temporal chunks and train a lightweight temporal saliency module that scores each chunk's contribution to the final answer. Second, we design a two-level reward: (1) a chunk-level intermediate reward that evaluates whether reasoning steps explicitly referencing specific temporal windows are factually grounded (verified via a frozen video-language model), and (2) the standard outcome reward. Third, we introduce a temporal consistency regularizer that penalizes contradictory reasoning about causally ordered events. We construct a new benchmark, LongVideoReason-50K, covering 5-60 minute videos with annotated temporal evidence spans.

Experiments: We evaluate on EgoSchema, LongVideoBench, Video-MME (long split), and LongVideoReason-50K. Ablations isolate contributions of chunk-level rewards vs. temporal consistency regularizer. Baselines include VideoRFT and standard GRPO without temporal decomposition.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning with Counterfactual Temporal Reasoning for Causal Video Understanding
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, MLLMs still struggle with counterfactual temporal reasoning—understanding what would happen if temporal order were disrupted or specific events were absent. This causal understanding gap limits deployment in safety-critical domains like autonomous driving and surgical video analysis.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, extending the RFT paradigm with counterfactual temporal augmentation. During SFT, we curate a CoT dataset where each sample includes both factual reasoning chains and counterfactual alternatives (e.g., 'If frame sequence were reversed, the causal chain would change because...'). We construct these via a structured perturbation pipeline: (1) temporal shuffling/reversal of video clips, (2) event masking at key causal junctures, and (3) an LLM-driven counterfactual CoT generator guided by causal graphs extracted from scene descriptions. During RL, we introduce a causal-consistency reward combining semantic alignment (from VideoRFT) with a counterfactual discriminability score—rewarding models that correctly distinguish factual from counterfactual temporal sequences.

Experiments: We evaluate on (1) existing benchmarks: NExT-QA causal subset, Causal-VidQA, EgoSchema; (2) a new CausalPerturb-Bench with systematically shuffled videos; (3) domain-specific tests on driving (nuScenes-QA) and procedural videos (CrossTask). Ablations isolate contributions of counterfactual CoTs versus causal reward.

title: TemporalCoT: Disentangling Temporal Order from Semantic Content in Video Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
description:
Problem: Existing video reasoning approaches like VideoRFT treat temporal reasoning implicitly within general CoT annotations, conflating 'what happens' with 'when and in what order it happens.' This leads to models that reason about video semantics but struggle with fine-grained temporal ordering, duration estimation, and causal sequencing—critical for tasks like procedure understanding, anomaly detection, and sports analysis.

Proposed Method: We propose TemporalCoT, which explicitly disentangles temporal structure from semantic content in video reasoning chains. We introduce a two-stream CoT format: (1) a Semantic Stream describing object states and events, and (2) a Temporal Structure Stream encoding relative ordering, duration ratios, and causal dependencies as structured temporal graphs. During RL fine-tuning, we design a Temporal Consistency Reward that penalizes violations of temporal order in generated reasoning (e.g., referencing an event before its timestamp) using lightweight temporal parsing. We curate TemporalCoT-50K by augmenting existing video QA datasets with automated temporal graph annotations extracted via timestamps and captions.

Experiments: We evaluate on temporal-heavy benchmarks (TemporalBench, EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, STAR), ablate stream contributions, compare against VideoRFT and standard CoT baselines, and analyze cases where temporal disentanglement corrects semantic hallucinations. We also test zero-shot transfer to procedural video understanding datasets like COIN and CrossTask.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward-Guided Temporal Grounding for Fine-Grained Event Localization in Video Reasoning
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT advances general video reasoning, it lacks explicit mechanisms to train models for precise temporal grounding — identifying exact timestamps where specific events occur. Current MLLMs struggle to answer questions like 'At what moment does the protagonist realize the deception?' requiring sub-second precision. Existing rewards focus on answer correctness but ignore temporal precision of supporting evidence.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, extending the RFT paradigm with a temporal grounding reward signal. During RL training, the model must output not only answers and CoT rationales but explicit temporal evidence spans (start/end timestamps). We design a dual reward: (1) a temporal IoU reward measuring overlap between predicted evidence spans and annotated ground-truth intervals, and (2) a causal coherence reward verifying that the reasoning chain references events in chronologically consistent order. We construct TemporalRFT-CoT-50K by augmenting existing dense video captioning datasets (ActivityNet-Captions, QVHighlights) with timestamp-linked CoT annotations generated via a pipeline combining automatic alignment tools with LLM revision.

Experiments: We evaluate on temporal grounding benchmarks (Charades-STA, NExT-GQA temporal splits), moment retrieval tasks, and existing VideoRFT benchmarks to verify no regression. Ablations isolate contributions of each reward component and test generalization to untrimmed long videos (EgoSchema).

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Causal and Counterfactual Temporal Reasoning in Videos
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT advances general video reasoning, it does not explicitly address a critical cognitive skill—counterfactual and causal temporal reasoning (e.g., 'What would have happened if action X occurred at timestamp T instead?'). Current MLLMs struggle to reason about hypothetical temporal interventions, a capability essential for robotics, autonomous driving, and medical video analysis.

Proposed Method: We design TemporalRFT, extending the RFT paradigm with a counterfactual-aware CoT pipeline. First, we construct a dataset by sampling real videos and using a causal reasoning LLM (e.g., DeepSeek-R1) to generate counterfactual scenarios grounded in structured video descriptions, producing plausible 'what-if' question-answer pairs with causal chain-of-thought annotations. A video MLLM then validates temporal consistency of generated CoTs against actual footage. During RL, we introduce a dual reward: (1) a causal-consistency reward measuring whether the model's counterfactual reasoning respects physical/temporal causality (verified via a pretrained event-causality model), and (2) the semantic-consistency reward from VideoRFT. 

Experiments: We evaluate on existing benchmarks (NExT-QA causal split, STAR), a newly constructed counterfactual video QA benchmark from Ego4D, and downstream tasks in robotic manipulation video understanding. We ablate each reward component and compare against VideoRFT and base MLLM baselines.

title: TemporalCRIT: Counterfactual Reasoning Incentivization for Temporal Causal Understanding in Video MLLMs
description: Problem: While VideoRFT improves video reasoning through chain-of-thought and semantic consistency rewards, it does not explicitly train models to understand counterfactual temporal causality — i.e., 'what would happen if event X had not occurred?' This higher-order causal reasoning is critical for applications like anomaly detection, surgical video analysis, and autonomous driving but remains untackled by current RFT approaches. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalCRIT, which augments the RFT pipeline with counterfactual video reasoning. First, we construct a counterfactual CoT dataset by prompting a reasoning LLM with structured video annotations to generate paired factual/counterfactual reasoning chains, then validate visual consistency via a MLLM. Second, we design a novel counterfactual consistency reward that scores model responses on (a) causal directionality accuracy — whether the model correctly identifies which events enable downstream outcomes — and (b) counterfactual coherence — whether the hypothesized alternative outcome is logically consistent with video physics. The RL phase trains the model using both VideoRFT-style semantic rewards and our new counterfactual rewards via GRPO. Experiments: We evaluate on existing benchmarks (EgoSchema, NExT-QA) plus a new counterfactual video QA benchmark we construct from Kinetics and Ego4D, measuring causal accuracy, hallucination rate, and out-of-distribution temporal generalization.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Dense Temporal Grounding via Timestamp-Anchored Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT advances video reasoning, it treats video understanding holistically without requiring models to precisely localize *when* specific events occur. Dense temporal grounding—identifying exact time intervals for complex, compositional queries—remains unsolved, yet is critical for applications like video surveillance, sports analytics, and medical procedure review. Current models hallucinate temporal positions or produce coarse estimates.

Proposed Method: We extend the RFT paradigm specifically for temporal grounding by designing timestamp-anchored CoT (TA-CoT), where reasoning chains explicitly interleave visual observations with predicted temporal intervals: e.g., '[0:03-0:07] subject enters frame → [0:09-0:15] interaction begins → answer: [0:09-0:22]'. We build a TA-CoT curation pipeline that extracts dense frame captions at regular intervals, prompts a reasoning LLM to construct temporally-structured chains, then validates timestamp accuracy against ground-truth annotations. For RL, we introduce a dual reward combining (1) temporal IoU reward measuring overlap between predicted and ground-truth intervals, and (2) a chain-coherence reward ensuring temporal ordering consistency within the reasoning trace.

Experiments: We evaluate on Charades-STA, ActivityNet-Captions, QVHighlights, and TACoS benchmarks. Ablations compare TA-CoT vs. standard CoT, individual reward components, and temporal resolution of frame sampling. We also test zero-shot transfer to egocentric video (Ego4D).

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning with Causal Interval Rewards for Long-Form Video Temporal Grounding
description: Problem: While VideoRFT advances general video reasoning, it lacks precise temporal localization capabilities—identifying *when* specific events occur across long videos (5–60 minutes). Current MLLMs struggle to produce accurate temporal grounding because chain-of-thought annotations rarely encode fine-grained interval reasoning, and existing reward functions don't penalize temporal mislocalization. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, extending the RFT paradigm with a specialized temporal grounding reward. First, we construct a CoT curation pipeline where reasoning chains explicitly include temporal hypotheses ('Event X likely occurs between timestamps T1-T2 because...') generated by prompting a reasoning LLM with dense video transcripts, ASR, and object tracking metadata. Second, during RL, we design a Causal Interval Reward (CIR) that combines: (1) IoU-based temporal precision scoring against ground-truth intervals, (2) causal consistency scoring that verifies temporal ordering of predicted events matches logical causality, and (3) a boundary sharpness bonus penalizing overly broad interval predictions. Experiments: We evaluate on ActivityNet-Causal, EgoSchema-Temporal, QVHighlights, and a new long-form benchmark we construct from documentary footage with human-annotated causal chains. We compare against VideoRFT, TimeChat, and VTimeLLM, reporting temporal IoU, reasoning coherence scores, and hallucination rates on multi-hop temporal questions.

title: TemporalCRF-RFT: Modeling Long-Range Temporal Dependencies in Video Reasoning via Conditional Random Field Reward Shaping
description:
Problem: VideoRFT treats video reasoning as a holistic process but struggles to capture long-range temporal dependencies where events separated by many frames causally influence each other (e.g., in instructional videos, sports strategy, or narrative films). The semantic-consistency reward in VideoRFT operates locally without explicitly modeling temporal ordering constraints across the reasoning chain.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalCRF-RFT, which augments the RL phase with a structured temporal reward derived from a lightweight Conditional Random Field (CRF) over the model's chain-of-thought segments. Each CoT sentence is aligned to a temporal video segment via cross-attention, and the CRF models pairwise transition potentials between adjacent and distant temporal segments. The reward signal penalizes temporally inconsistent reasoning (e.g., referencing a later event before an earlier one, or violating causal ordering) while encouraging globally coherent temporal narratives. We additionally introduce a temporal contrastive auxiliary loss during SFT that trains the model to distinguish correctly-ordered CoTs from shuffled counterparts.

Experiments: We evaluate on temporally demanding benchmarks (EgoSchema, TemporalBench, MovieChat-1K, and ActivityNet-QA), constructing a new split requiring multi-hop temporal reasoning across >60 second videos. Ablations compare local vs. global CRF reward scopes and measure temporal ordering accuracy as a novel diagnostic metric.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward Shaping via Temporal Grounding Verification for Video Reasoning
description:
Problem: VideoRFT improves video reasoning but treats temporal localization implicitly—models may arrive at correct answers through superficial pattern matching rather than genuine temporal understanding (e.g., correctly answering 'what happened before X' without identifying when X occurs). Current semantic-consistency rewards don't explicitly verify that reasoning chains correctly localize evidence in time.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RL reward with a temporal grounding verification (TGV) component. During RL training, we require models to produce not only chain-of-thought reasoning but explicit temporal evidence citations (e.g., 'at frames 45-60, the subject...'), which are automatically verified against ground-truth temporal annotations using IoU-based grounding scores. The composite reward combines: (1) answer correctness, (2) semantic consistency from VideoRFT, and (3) temporal grounding IoU reward. We also construct a temporal-grounding-annotated RL dataset (TG-150K) by augmenting existing video QA datasets with frame-level evidence spans via automated annotation using video captioning models.

Experiments: We evaluate on temporal reasoning benchmarks (NExT-QA, EgoTimeQA, TimeIT), compare against VideoRFT and standard GRPO baselines, ablate individual reward components, and measure whether temporal citation quality correlates with downstream accuracy improvements. We also test generalization on out-of-distribution temporal reasoning tasks to assess whether explicit grounding provides transferable benefits.

title: TemporalChain: Reward-Guided Temporal Grounding for Video Reasoning via Process-Level Verification
description: Problem: VideoRFT and similar approaches apply outcome-based rewards that evaluate final answer correctness, but they lack fine-grained supervision over the intermediate temporal reasoning steps (e.g., correctly identifying which frames support a causal claim). Models can produce correct answers via spurious shortcuts without genuinely grounding reasoning in the right temporal evidence. Method: We propose TemporalChain, which introduces a process reward model (PRM) specifically designed for video temporal reasoning. Instead of only rewarding final answers, TemporalChain rewards each reasoning step by verifying (1) temporal consistency — whether cited timestamps/segments actually contain the claimed visual evidence, and (2) causal ordering — whether the inferred event sequence respects the true temporal order in the video. We train a lightweight temporal verifier using contrastive learning on frame-step alignment pairs, then integrate it as a dense step-level reward signal into GRPO training. Experiments: We evaluate on VideoRFT benchmarks (EgoSchema, MVBench, Video-MME, TemporalBench) plus a new diagnostic split that tests robustness to temporal permutation attacks (shuffled frames). Ablations compare outcome-only vs. process-only vs. combined rewards. We also measure hallucination rates on temporal claims and analyze whether PRM guidance reduces temporal shortcut exploitation compared to VideoRFT baselines.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning with Counterfactual Temporal Reasoning for Causal Video Understanding
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, models still struggle with fine-grained temporal causality — understanding *why* events occur in a specific order and what would happen if the order changed. Existing benchmarks and rewards don't explicitly probe counterfactual temporal reasoning (e.g., 'If action A happened before B instead of after, what would the outcome be?').

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT pipeline with counterfactual temporal reasoning. (1) We construct a counterfactual CoT dataset by automatically generating temporally-permuted video clips and asking a reasoning LLM to contrast outcomes under different orderings, yielding ~50K counterfactual SFT examples. (2) During RL, we design a dual reward: a standard correctness reward plus a counterfactual consistency reward that penalizes models whose causal explanations contradict their predicted outcomes under temporal permutations. (3) We introduce a new benchmark, CounterTemp-QA, with 3K human-annotated counterfactual temporal reasoning questions spanning cooking, sports, and procedural domains.

Experiments: We compare TemporalRFT against VideoRFT and other baselines on CounterTemp-QA, existing causal video QA benchmarks (NExT-QA, Causal-VidQA), and standard video reasoning benchmarks to verify no regression, ablating each reward component.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward Shaping for Fine-Grained Temporal Grounding in Video Reasoning via Timestamp-Anchored Chain-of-Thought
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, it treats temporal localization as implicit. MLLMs still struggle to pinpoint *when* specific events occur and to reason causally across precise temporal intervals—a critical gap for applications like procedure understanding, anomaly detection, and sports analysis.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT pipeline with explicit temporal grounding. First, we extend CoT annotations to include timestamp-anchored reasoning steps (e.g., '[0:12-0:18]: agent picks up object → causes [0:25]: door opens'), constructing a 50K dataset via automated pipeline combining ASR, optical flow keyframe detection, and a reasoning LLM. Second, we design two complementary rewards: (1) a temporal-IoU reward that scores predicted event spans against ground-truth timestamps, and (2) a causal-chain consistency reward that verifies temporal ordering of reasoning steps is monotonically consistent. Third, we introduce a curriculum training schedule that progressively increases video length during RL training to build robust long-horizon temporal reasoning.

Experiments: We evaluate on Charades-STA, ActivityNet-Causal, NExT-QA temporal splits, and a new benchmark TemporalCausal-Bench (1K hand-annotated temporal causal questions). Ablations isolate contributions of each reward component and curriculum scheduling. We compare against VideoRFT, TimeChat, and VTimeLLM baselines.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Causal and Counterfactual Video Reasoning via Temporal Intervention Rewards
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT advances general video reasoning, models still struggle with explicitly causal and counterfactual reasoning—understanding 'what would happen if X had not occurred' or 'why did Y happen before Z.' These temporal intervention questions require models to disentangle causal chains rather than recognize surface patterns, yet no targeted training signal exists for this capability.

Proposed Method: We extend the RFT paradigm with a Temporal Intervention Reward (TIR) that explicitly evaluates causal reasoning quality. First, we construct CausalVideoQA-50K, a dataset of counterfactual and causal intervention questions generated by prompting a reasoning LLM with structured event graphs extracted from videos, then verified by human annotators. Second, during RL training, beyond standard outcome-correctness rewards, we introduce TIR: a reward that measures whether the model's reasoning chain correctly identifies causal antecedents by checking logical consistency between the proposed cause, intervened counterfactual scenario, and predicted outcome using a lightweight causal-graph verifier. Third, we augment the CoT curation pipeline with explicit counterfactual branches ('if event A had not happened, then...') to improve SFT initialization.

Experiments: We evaluate on NExT-QA (causal/temporal splits), CLEVRER, EgoSchema causal subset, and our new CausalVideoQA benchmark. Ablations isolate contributions of TIR vs. semantic-consistency reward from VideoRFT, demonstrating improved causal disentanglement without sacrificing general video reasoning performance.

title: TemporalCoT-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Causal-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness in Video Reasoning MLLMs
description: Problem: While VideoRFT improves video reasoning via reinforced fine-tuning, it remains unclear whether the generated chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning traces are actually faithful to the temporal and causal structure of videos, or merely post-hoc rationalizations that happen to produce correct answers. Existing benchmarks evaluate final answer accuracy without probing whether intermediate reasoning steps correctly identify temporal ordering, causal relationships, and event durations. Method: We propose (1) TemporalCoT-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark with 5K video QA instances annotated with ground-truth causal-temporal reasoning graphs, enabling step-level faithfulness evaluation via graph-matching metrics; and (2) a Temporal-Causal Consistency (TCC) reward for RL training that penalizes reasoning steps that violate temporal ordering or causal direction detectable from video timestamps and optical flow signals. The TCC reward complements semantic rewards by explicitly grounding intermediate CoT steps to verifiable temporal anchors extracted automatically from video metadata. Experiments: We evaluate VideoRFT and other video MLLMs on TemporalCoT-Bench, measuring step-level faithfulness vs. answer accuracy trade-offs. We then apply TCC reward augmentation to VideoRFT's RL phase and measure improvements on both faithfulness metrics and downstream benchmarks (EgoSchema, NeXT-QA, Video-MME), demonstrating that faithful temporal reasoning transfers to better generalization.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward Shaping via Temporal Grounding Consistency for Video Reasoning
description: Problem: VideoRFT improves video reasoning but treats video understanding holistically, lacking explicit supervision that forces models to correctly identify *when* in a video specific evidence occurs. Models can generate plausible-sounding reasoning chains that cite incorrect temporal segments, a subtle form of hallucination not penalized by semantic-consistency rewards alone. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RL phase with a Temporal Grounding Consistency (TGC) reward. During RL rollouts, we prompt the model to produce reasoning chains that include explicit temporal citations (e.g., '[0:12-0:18]: subject picks up object'). A lightweight temporal verifier—trained on existing temporal grounding datasets (QVHighlights, Charades-STA)—checks whether cited intervals genuinely contain the claimed visual evidence. The TGC reward is a continuous score from this verifier, combined with answer correctness, penalizing temporally misattributed reasoning. We also construct a temporal-citation SFT dataset (TemporalCoT-50K) using automated pipeline: extract ground-truth temporal annotations from existing QA datasets and inject interval markers into CoT chains. Experiments: We evaluate on EgoSchema, NExT-QA, MVBench, and introduce a new Temporal Attribution Accuracy metric measuring citation correctness. Ablations compare TGC reward vs. semantic-consistency reward vs. combined. We expect gains on temporally-sensitive benchmarks (+3-5%) with reduced temporal hallucination rates.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Causal and Counterfactual Temporal Reasoning in Videos
description: Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, it does not explicitly target causal and counterfactual temporal reasoning — i.e., understanding 'why' events occur and 'what would happen if' a prior event changed. These abilities are critical for applications like accident analysis, surgical procedure understanding, and social interaction modeling, yet current benchmarks and training signals inadequately capture them. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the VideoRFT framework with two targeted components. First, we construct a Causal-Counterfactual CoT dataset (CC-CoT-50K) by prompting a reasoning LLM with structured event graphs extracted from videos, then asking it to generate chains-of-thought that explicitly include causal attribution steps and counterfactual hypotheticals ('If action A had not occurred at t=3s, then...'). Second, we design a Causal-Consistency Reward that scores RL rollouts by verifying whether stated causal links are temporally ordered correctly and whether counterfactual conclusions contradict factual video evidence, using a lightweight temporal-graph verifier. Experiments: We evaluate on existing benchmarks (NExT-QA, Causal-VidQA, EgoSchema) and introduce a new counterfactual video QA benchmark with human annotations across three domains (cooking, sports, social). Ablations isolate contributions of causal CoT data vs. the causal-consistency reward.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward-Guided Temporal Grounding for Video Reasoning via Timestamp-Anchored Chain-of-Thought
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT advances video reasoning through CoT and RL, it lacks explicit mechanisms to ground reasoning steps to specific temporal intervals. Models may produce plausible-sounding reasoning chains that reference video content without accurately localizing when events occur, leading to temporally ungrounded hallucinations that standard semantic-consistency rewards cannot penalize.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT paradigm with timestamp-anchored CoT annotations and a novel temporal grounding reward. During SFT, we extend the CoT curation pipeline to require each reasoning step to cite supporting temporal spans (e.g., '[t=12s-18s] the character picks up the object'). During RL, we design a dual reward: (1) a temporal precision reward that scores overlap between model-cited timestamps and ground-truth event intervals using soft-IoU, and (2) the semantic-consistency reward from VideoRFT. A lightweight temporal verifier module extracts and evaluates timestamp citations from generated reasoning chains without requiring human annotation at RL time.

Experiments: We evaluate on NExT-QA, EgoSchema, Charades-STA, and ActivityNet-QA, measuring both QA accuracy and temporal grounding precision. Ablations isolate the contribution of timestamp-anchored SFT vs. temporal reward. We additionally test temporal reasoning robustness by shuffling frame order, demonstrating that TemporalRFT learns genuinely temporal rather than semantic shortcuts.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward Shaping via Fine-Grained Temporal Localization for Video Reasoning
description: Problem: VideoRFT improves general video reasoning but treats temporal grounding as implicit — the model is not explicitly rewarded for correctly identifying *when* in the video evidence occurs. This leads to temporally mislocalized reasoning chains that happen to produce correct answers by coincidence, limiting interpretability and robustness on temporally demanding tasks (e.g., procedural QA, causal event ordering, anomaly detection). Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RL reward signal with a temporal localization reward. During RL, the model must emit structured CoTs containing explicit temporal citations (e.g., '[t=12s–18s]: the person picks up the knife'). We design a dual reward: (1) a standard answer-correctness reward, and (2) a temporal precision reward computed by comparing model-cited timestamps against automatically extracted pseudo-ground-truth intervals via an off-the-shelf video grounding model (e.g., TimeChat or UniVTG). The combined reward incentivizes both correct answers and temporally faithful reasoning. We also construct a temporal-CoT SFT seed dataset by augmenting VideoRFT-CoT-102K with timestamp annotations using video grounding models. Experiments: We evaluate on TemporalBench, EgoSchema, NExT-QA, and Causal-VidQA, plus a new temporal faithfulness metric measuring citation precision/recall. Ablations isolate the contribution of the temporal reward vs. baseline VideoRFT.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Causal and Counterfactual Video Reasoning via Temporal Graph Rewards
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, it does not explicitly address causal and counterfactual reasoning ('What would happen if X had not occurred?'), which requires models to construct and query explicit temporal causal graphs rather than sequential narration chains. Current CoT pipelines treat video reasoning as forward-only inference, leaving counterfactual and interventional reasoning largely unsupported.

Proposed Method: We extend the RFT paradigm with two innovations. First, we introduce a Temporal Causal Graph (TCG) CoT format, where reasoning chains explicitly encode causal nodes (events), directed edges (causal links), and counterfactual branches annotated by a reasoning LLM guided by causal templates. Second, we design a graph-consistency reward for the RL phase that scores the model's reasoning by verifying (1) topological consistency of predicted causal chains against a reference TCG extracted by a specialist model, and (2) counterfactual plausibility via interventional simulation on the graph.

Experiments: We curate a 50K TCG-CoT dataset from Ego4D and Something-Something-v2. We evaluate on existing benchmarks (NExT-QA causal split, STAR) and a new CounterVideo-QA benchmark we construct via human annotation of counterfactual scenarios. Ablations isolate the contribution of TCG-CoT format vs. graph-consistency reward vs. baseline VideoRFT training.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward Shaping via Temporal Grounding Consistency for Long-Form Video Reasoning
description:
Problem: VideoRFT improves general video reasoning but treats temporal localization implicitly. For long-form videos (>5 minutes), models still struggle to ground reasoning steps to precise temporal segments, leading to temporally incoherent chains-of-thought where the model references events out of order or fabricates temporal relationships.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RFT framework with explicit temporal grounding supervision. First, we extend the CoT curation pipeline to annotate each reasoning step with timestamp intervals (e.g., 'At 0:32–0:45, the character picks up the key, which causes...'), creating a temporally-anchored CoT dataset of 50K long-form videos from MovieChat, EgoSchema, and ActivityNet. Second, we design a composite reward comprising: (1) a temporal ordering reward penalizing violations of event chronology in the reasoning chain, (2) a temporal precision reward measuring IoU between model-predicted temporal references and ground-truth intervals, and (3) the semantic consistency reward from VideoRFT. The RL policy is trained to jointly optimize answer correctness and temporal grounding fidelity.

Experiments: We evaluate on EgoSchema, MovieChat-1K, LLaVA-Video-Bench (long), and introduce a new Temporal Coherence Score metric. Ablations isolate each reward component's contribution. We compare against VideoRFT and other baselines across video lengths (1–30 min).

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Causal and Counterfactual Video Reasoning via Temporal Intervention Rewards
description: Problem: While VideoRFT advances general video reasoning, models still struggle with explicitly causal and counterfactual reasoning—understanding not just 'what happened' but 'why' and 'what would have happened if X were different.' Current reward signals treat temporal reasoning superficially, failing to distinguish genuine causal understanding from spurious correlations. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, extending the RFT paradigm with a temporal intervention reward that probes causal understanding. During RL training, for each video QA instance, we automatically generate counterfactual variants by (1) masking or reordering critical temporal segments and (2) asking the model to predict outcomes under these interventions. The reward function combines: (a) correctness on original questions, (b) consistency of causal explanations under temporal perturbations (answers should change predictably when causal segments are removed), and (c) a contrastive chain-of-thought coherence score comparing reasoning across original vs. counterfactual inputs. We curate a CounterfactualVideo-50K dataset using LLM-driven causal graph extraction from existing video datasets. Experiments: We evaluate on CLEVRER, Next-QA causal splits, Causal-VidQA, and a new counterfactual probing benchmark we construct. We compare against VideoRFT and ablate each reward component, demonstrating improved causal disentanglement without sacrificing general video QA performance.

title: TemporalChain: Self-Improving Video Reasoning via Counterfactual Temporal Augmentation and Process Reward Modeling
description:
Problem: VideoRFT improves video reasoning via CoT curation and outcome-based semantic rewards, but struggles with temporal reasoning failures where models identify correct answers through spurious spatial cues rather than genuine temporal understanding. Current reward signals cannot distinguish models that truly reason over time from those exploiting single-frame shortcuts.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalChain, which augments the RFT pipeline with two innovations: (1) Counterfactual Temporal Augmentation (CTA) — automatically generating temporally-perturbed video variants (frame shuffling, speed alteration, segment removal) paired with contrastive CoT annotations that explicitly explain why temporal order matters, forcing models to internalize causal-temporal structure; (2) Temporal Process Reward Model (T-PRM) — a lightweight reward model trained to score intermediate reasoning steps specifically for temporal coherence, assigning step-level rewards based on whether each reasoning step correctly references temporal relationships (before/after/during/causes) consistent with video evidence, rather than only evaluating final answers.

Experiments: We evaluate on temporal-heavy benchmarks (NExT-QA, EgoSchema, Perception Test, ActivityNet-QA) and construct a new diagnostic benchmark, TemporalBias-Eval, measuring single-frame shortcut exploitation. Ablations compare outcome-only rewards vs. T-PRM process rewards, and standard CoT vs. counterfactually-augmented CoT. We demonstrate improved temporal reasoning generalization with reduced single-frame bias.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning with Counterfactual Temporal Reasoning Rewards for Causal Video Understanding
description: Problem: While VideoRFT advances video reasoning via chain-of-thought and semantic consistency rewards, it does not explicitly train models to distinguish genuine causal-temporal relationships from spurious correlations. Models may learn to answer correctly by exploiting static visual cues rather than understanding event causality and temporal ordering. Method: We propose TemporalRFT, which augments the RL phase with a counterfactual temporal reasoning reward. During training, for each video we automatically construct counterfactual variants by: (1) temporally shuffling key event segments, (2) reversing causal subsequences, and (3) replacing causal events with visually similar but causally irrelevant alternatives. The reward function penalizes models that give consistent answers across original and counterfactual variants when they should differ, and rewards models that correctly differentiate them. We combine this with a temporal grounding auxiliary loss that forces the reasoning chain to explicitly cite timestamps supporting causal claims. We curate a 50K counterfactual augmentation dataset using automated video editing pipelines paired with GPT-4o verification. Experiments: We evaluate on NExT-QA, Causal-VidQA, EgoSchema, and a new Counterfactual Temporal Reasoning benchmark we construct, comparing against VideoRFT and other baselines. Ablations isolate each counterfactual perturbation type and the grounding loss contribution.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning with Counterfactual Temporal Rewards for Causal Video Reasoning
description: Problem: While VideoRFT advances video reasoning via chain-of-thought and semantic consistency rewards, it does not explicitly disentangle causal from correlational reasoning in temporal sequences. Models may learn spurious shortcuts (e.g., scene context) rather than genuine cause-effect understanding across frames. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RL phase with counterfactual temporal rewards. During training, we automatically generate counterfactual video variants by frame-order shuffling, event segment removal, or causal-break injection (swapping cause and effect clips). The reward function penalizes models that maintain high confidence on counterfactually-manipulated videos where the causal chain is broken, while rewarding confident correct answers on intact videos. This temporal contrastive reward is combined with a fine-grained temporal grounding reward that scores whether the model's CoT correctly references specific temporal intervals. We construct a Causal-Video-50K benchmark with human-annotated cause-effect question pairs and corresponding counterfactual variants across domains (cooking, sports, physical events). Experiments: We compare against VideoRFT and baselines on (1) existing benchmarks (NeXT-QA causal subset, EgoSchema), (2) Causal-Video-50K, and (3) out-of-distribution causal reasoning in procedural domains. Ablations isolate contributions of counterfactual vs. grounding rewards.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Dense Temporal Grounding and Event Localization in Long-Form Videos
description:
Problem: VideoRFT advances general video reasoning but struggles with precise temporal grounding in long-form videos (>10 minutes), where models must pinpoint when specific events occur rather than just what happens. Current MLLMs produce temporally vague reasoning ('this happens early in the video') rather than precise timestamp-grounded answers.

Proposed Method: We extend the RFT paradigm specifically for temporal localization reasoning. First, we construct a CoT dataset (TemporalCoT-50K) where reasoning chains explicitly include timestamp hypotheses, elimination of candidate intervals, and temporal anchoring steps, curated from long-form instructional and documentary videos. Second, we design a temporal-precision reward function combining: (1) interval-overlap reward (tIoU between predicted and ground-truth temporal spans), (2) temporal ordering consistency reward penalizing contradictory timestamp references within a reasoning chain, and (3) the semantic-consistency reward from VideoRFT adapted for temporal context windows. During RL training, we sample diverse temporal queries requiring multi-hop temporal reasoning (e.g., 'What happens 30 seconds after the presenter mentions X?').

Experiments: Evaluate on Ego4D NLQ, ActivityNet-Causal, QVHighlights, and a new long-form benchmark we construct. Ablations isolate contributions of each reward component. Compare against VideoRFT, TimeChat, and VTimeLLM baselines to demonstrate temporal grounding superiority.

title: TemporalContrastRFT: Contrastive Temporal Reward Shaping for Fine-Grained Video Causal Reasoning
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT advances video reasoning via semantic-consistency rewards, it treats temporal structure implicitly. Models still struggle with fine-grained causal reasoning — distinguishing *why* an event occurred versus *what* happened, and correctly ordering causally-linked events across long temporal spans. Existing rewards don't penalize models that produce correct conclusions via temporally scrambled reasoning chains.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalContrastRFT, which augments RL training with a Contrastive Temporal Reward (CTR). During RL rollouts, we generate 'temporal foil' reasoning chains by shuffling causal steps in the model's CoT outputs while preserving semantic content. A reward model trained on temporally-annotated video captions scores the original versus foiled chains, and the CTR is defined as the margin between these scores. This incentivizes the model to produce causally-ordered, temporally-coherent reasoning rather than bag-of-events descriptions. We additionally curate a CausalVideoRFT-50K dataset with explicit temporal dependency annotations using automated scene graph extraction and LLM-based causal labeling.

Experiments: (1) Evaluate on NExT-QA, Causal-VidQA, and EgoSchema benchmarks focusing on causal/temporal question types; (2) Ablations comparing CTR vs. semantic-consistency reward vs. combination; (3) Human evaluation of causal coherence in reasoning chains; (4) Stress-test on adversarial temporally-shuffled video inputs to measure robustness of learned temporal grounding.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Dense Temporal Grounding via Process-Level Rewards in Video MLLMs
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, it treats temporal localization as implicit — models rarely produce precise timestamp predictions as part of their reasoning chains. Dense temporal grounding (localizing when specific events occur) remains a bottleneck, yet is critical for applications like video surveillance, sports analysis, and procedural understanding. Existing RFT rewards operate at answer-level outcome quality, providing no fine-grained signal about temporal precision during the reasoning process.

Proposed Method: We propose TemporalRFT, extending RFT with process-level temporal rewards. First, we construct a CoT dataset (~80K clips) where reasoning chains explicitly include timestamp hypotheses at intermediate steps ('Event X likely occurs between t=12s-15s because...'). We then design a composite reward: (1) a temporal IoU reward comparing predicted temporal intervals against ground-truth annotations, (2) a causal ordering reward penalizing temporally inconsistent reasoning chains, and (3) the standard answer correctness reward. We use GRPO to jointly optimize these signals, encouraging the model to interleave spatial-visual evidence with temporal predictions throughout its chain-of-thought.

Experiments: Evaluate on Charades-STA, ActivityNet-Captions, QVHighlights, and TACoS for temporal grounding; VideoMME and MVBench for general reasoning. Ablations isolate contributions of each reward component. We demonstrate that explicit temporal process rewards improve both grounding precision and downstream QA accuracy by forcing temporally-coherent reasoning.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward-Guided Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Dense Temporal Grounding in Long-Form Videos
description: Problem: While VideoRFT advances general video reasoning, it lacks explicit mechanisms for precise temporal grounding—identifying exact time intervals where specific events, causes, or evidence occur in long-form videos (>10 minutes). Current MLLMs struggle to produce temporally-anchored reasoning chains that cite specific timestamps, limiting interpretability and downstream utility in applications like video editing, surveillance, and sports analytics. Proposed Method: We extend the RFT paradigm with a temporal grounding reward signal. First, we construct a CoT dataset (TemporalRFT-CoT-50K) where reasoning chains explicitly reference timestamp spans using a structured format: <think>Evidence at [t1,t2]: ...</think><answer>...</answer>. Second, we introduce a dual reward during RL training: (1) a temporal-IoU reward comparing predicted timestamp spans against ground-truth annotations, and (2) the existing semantic-consistency reward from VideoRFT. To curate training data, we leverage existing temporal grounding datasets (QVHighlights, ActivityNet-Captions) augmented with LLM-generated causal reasoning chains. We adopt a sliding-window visual tokenization strategy to handle long-form video context efficiently. Experiments: We evaluate on Charades-STA, QVHighlights, ActivityNet-Captions, and a new long-form reasoning benchmark we construct from documentary footage, measuring R@1, mIoU, and a novel reasoning-grounding alignment score. Ablations isolate contributions of each reward component.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward Shaping via Temporal Grounding Consistency for Fine-Grained Video Reasoning
description:
Problem: VideoRFT improves general video reasoning but treats temporal localization as implicit — the model is not explicitly rewarded for correctly identifying *when* in the video the evidence for its reasoning occurs. This leads to temporally ungrounded reasoning chains that may produce correct answers via spurious correlations rather than genuine temporal understanding.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RL phase with a Temporal Grounding Consistency (TGC) reward. During training, for each reasoning chain generated by the MLLM, we use a lightweight temporal grounding module (e.g., fine-tuned VideoLLaMA) to extract predicted temporal segments referenced in the chain-of-thought. The TGC reward measures overlap (temporal IoU) between these predicted segments and ground-truth temporal annotations. We combine TGC with answer-correctness and semantic-consistency rewards via a learned weighting scheme trained to maximize held-out benchmark performance. Additionally, we construct a temporally-annotated CoT dataset (Temporal-CoT-40K) by extending VideoRFT's pipeline with automated temporal span labeling using off-the-shelf moment retrieval models.

Experiments: We evaluate on Temporal-sensitive benchmarks (NExT-QA, Causal-VidQA, ActivityNet-QA temporal splits, EgoSchema), comparing against VideoRFT and ablations removing TGC reward. We also measure temporal localization accuracy to verify improved grounding drives reasoning gains rather than answer shortcuts.

title: TemporalRewardRFT: Fine-Grained Temporal Grounding Rewards for Video Reasoning via Timestamp-Anchored Chain-of-Thought
description: Problem: VideoRFT's semantic-consistency reward operates at the answer level but does not explicitly enforce that intermediate reasoning steps are temporally grounded—a model can produce correct answers by reasoning about wrong time intervals. This leads to brittle reasoning that fails on temporally complex queries (e.g., causal event ordering, procedure understanding). Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRewardRFT, which augments the RFT pipeline with timestamp-anchored CoT annotations and a temporal grounding reward. During SFT, we extend CoT curation to include explicit frame/timestamp citations for each reasoning step (e.g., '[t=12s] The character picks up the knife, causing...'). During RL, we add a temporal grounding reward computed by (1) extracting cited timestamps from generated CoTs via regex parsing, (2) retrieving corresponding frames, and (3) scoring visual-textual alignment of the cited evidence using a lightweight CLIP-based verifier. The final reward combines VideoRFT's outcome reward, semantic-consistency reward, and our temporal grounding reward with learned coefficients. Experiments: We evaluate on NExT-QA, TemporalBench, Causal-VidQA, and EgoSchema, with ablations isolating each reward component. We further analyze whether temporal grounding correlates with answer accuracy and generalization to unseen video lengths, demonstrating that explicit temporal self-citation improves both interpretability and performance.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Counterfactual and Causal Video Reasoning via Interventional Chain-of-Thought
description: Problem: While VideoRFT advances general video reasoning, models still struggle with counterfactual and causal reasoning—understanding not just what happened but why, and what would have happened under different conditions. This higher-order reasoning is critical for applications like autonomous driving, medical video analysis, and procedural understanding, yet no existing benchmark or training paradigm explicitly targets it. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which extends VideoRFT's RFT paradigm with a focus on interventional reasoning. We construct a Counterfactual Video CoT dataset (CF-VideoCoT-80K) by augmenting existing video datasets with synthetically perturbed clips (object removal, action substitution, temporal reordering) using video editing models, paired with counterfactual CoT annotations generated via a causal prompting strategy that explicitly asks 'what changes if X were different?' We design a causal consistency reward that penalizes reasoning chains violating do-calculus principles (e.g., contradicting known causal directions) and rewards correct identification of minimal causal interventions. Experiments: We evaluate on existing benchmarks (NExT-QA, Causal-VidQA, STAR) and propose a new Counterfactual Video Reasoning benchmark (CVR-Bench) with 5K human-annotated counterfactual questions across 4 domains. Ablations examine reward components, intervention types, and cross-domain transfer to medical and driving videos.

title: TemporalRFT: Reward Shaping via Fine-Grained Temporal Grounding for Video Reasoning
description: Problem: While VideoRFT advances video reasoning through chain-of-thought and semantic-consistency rewards, it treats temporal localization as implicit. Models may arrive at correct answers without genuinely grounding reasoning steps to specific video timestamps, limiting interpretability and robustness on temporally dense tasks (e.g., procedure understanding, causal event ordering, anomaly detection). Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which augments the RL phase with an explicit temporal grounding reward. During training, each CoT reasoning step is required to cite a temporal interval [t_start, t_end] supporting the inference. We design a composite reward: (1) a correctness reward on final answers, (2) a temporal precision reward measuring IoU between cited intervals and ground-truth event segments from automated video annotation tools (e.g., dense video captioners + moment retrieval models), and (3) a temporal consistency reward penalizing contradictory or out-of-order timestamp citations across reasoning steps. We also construct a temporally-annotated RL dataset (TemporalRFT-RL-150K) by augmenting existing video QA corpora with automated temporal segment labels. Experiments: We evaluate on temporal reasoning benchmarks (NExT-QA, EgoTaskQA, ActivityNet-QA, TemporalBench), ablating each reward component and comparing against VideoRFT. We further analyze whether temporal grounding citations improve human-interpretable faithfulness via human evaluation.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Dense Temporal Grounding and Event Localization in Long-Form Videos
description:
Problem: VideoRFT improves general video reasoning but does not explicitly address dense temporal grounding — the ability to precisely localize when events occur in long-form videos (>10 minutes). Current MLLMs struggle to produce accurate timestamps and temporal chains of causality across hundreds of frames, limiting utility in applications like surveillance analysis, sports analytics, and documentary understanding.

Proposed Method: We extend the RFT paradigm with a temporally-aware CoT framework. First, we construct a CoT curation pipeline that generates timestamp-anchored reasoning chains: each reasoning step explicitly references predicted temporal intervals (e.g., '[0:32-0:45]: subject picks up object, causing...'), validated against ground-truth temporal annotations. Second, we introduce two novel RL rewards: (1) a temporal IoU reward measuring overlap between predicted and ground-truth event intervals, and (2) a causal-ordering reward penalizing logically inconsistent temporal sequences. Third, we incorporate a frame-sampling curriculum that gradually increases video length during RL training, forcing the model to develop long-range temporal attention.

Experiments: We evaluate on ActivityNet-Captions, QVHighlights, Ego4D-NLQ, and a new long-form benchmark we construct from documentary footage. Ablations isolate contributions of timestamp-anchored CoTs, each reward component, and the length curriculum. We compare against VideoRFT and dedicated temporal grounding models.

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning with Timestamp-Grounded Rewards for Dense Video Event Localization and Reasoning
description:
Problem: While VideoRFT improves general video reasoning, it lacks fine-grained temporal grounding — models cannot precisely localize *when* reasoning-relevant events occur within long videos. This limits applicability to tasks like procedure understanding, anomaly detection, and video question answering requiring exact temporal evidence citation.

Proposed Method: We extend the RFT paradigm with timestamp-grounded reasoning chains and a novel temporal localization reward. During SFT, we curate a dataset (TempCoT-50K) where each CoT step includes explicit timestamp intervals justifying each reasoning step, generated via a pipeline combining speech transcripts, dense captions at 1fps, and a reasoning LLM. During RL, we introduce two complementary rewards: (1) a temporal precision reward measuring IoU between model-predicted evidence timestamps and ground-truth event boundaries, and (2) a causal ordering reward penalizing reasoning chains where cited temporal evidence violates chronological consistency. A lightweight temporal attention module is added to the MLLM to explicitly aggregate frame-level features at predicted intervals before generating each reasoning step.

Experiments: Evaluate on temporal grounding benchmarks (Charades-STA, ActivityNet-Captions), procedural QA (COIN, ProceduralVQA), and long-video reasoning (EgoSchema, Video-MME-Long). Ablations isolate contributions of timestamp supervision, each reward component, and temporal attention module. Baselines include VideoRFT and specialist temporal grounding models.

title: TemporalChain: Reward-Guided Temporal Grounding for Video Reasoning via Step-Level Process Reward Models
description:
Problem: VideoRFT and similar approaches use outcome-based rewards (final answer correctness, semantic consistency) but neglect whether intermediate reasoning steps correctly localize evidence temporally. A model may produce correct answers through temporally incoherent reasoning chains that hallucinate which video segments support each inference step. This undermines trustworthiness and generalization to temporal reasoning tasks.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalChain, which trains a step-level Process Reward Model (PRM) specifically for video reasoning. Given a CoT chain, each reasoning step is annotated with a temporal grounding score measuring alignment between the step's claims and specific video timestamps/segments (verified via an off-the-shelf temporal grounding model like VTimeLLM). During GRPO-style RL training, we augment the scalar outcome reward with dense per-step temporal grounding rewards, penalizing steps that cite incorrect temporal evidence. We construct a PRM training dataset by sampling VideoRFT-style chains, automatically annotating per-step temporal correctness using timestamp verification heuristics and human spot-checking.

Experiments: (1) Compare against VideoRFT and outcome-reward-only baselines on temporal reasoning benchmarks (NExT-QA, ActivityNet-QA, EgoSchema, Charades-STA). (2) Ablate step-level vs. outcome-only rewards. (3) Evaluate temporal hallucination rates using a new metric: Temporal Evidence Faithfulness (TEF) measuring step-timestamp alignment in generated chains. (4) Analyze generalization to unseen video domains (surgical videos, sports).

title: TemporalRFT: Reinforced Fine-Tuning for Procedural Step Localization and Causal Chain Reasoning in Instructional Videos
description: Problem: While VideoRFT advances general video reasoning, instructional videos (cooking, surgery, assembly) demand a specialized capability: precisely localizing procedural steps and inferring causal dependencies between them (e.g., 'step B failed because step A was skipped'). Current MLLMs struggle to jointly perform temporal grounding and causal chain reasoning in these structured, domain-rich scenarios. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalRFT, which extends the RFT paradigm with three innovations: (1) a procedural CoT schema that decomposes reasoning into step-detection, temporal boundary prediction, and causal dependency annotation; (2) a dual reward signal combining timestamp-accuracy reward (IoU between predicted and ground-truth step boundaries) with a causal-graph consistency reward that checks whether the inferred dependency graph matches expert-annotated causal structures; (3) a step-contrastive RL objective that penalizes reasoning chains that correctly identify steps but assign wrong causal relationships. We construct ProceduralRFT-CoT-50K from HowTo100M and CholecT50 (surgical) using GPT-4o with structured procedure templates. Experiments: We evaluate on temporal grounding benchmarks (Charades-STA, ActivityNet-Captions), procedural understanding (COIN, CrossTask), and a new causal-step QA benchmark we construct. Ablations isolate contributions of each reward component and the procedural CoT schema.
